---
title: "Generalizable PheNorm Analysis"
author: "PheNormBox user"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%Y-%m-%d')`"
knit: (function(inputFile, encoding) {
  name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(inputFile));
  project <- dirname(normalizePath(inputFile));
  out <- file.path(project, "Result", paste0(
    name, "_result_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
  ));
  dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE);
  Sys.setenv(RUN_DIR = out);
  on.exit(Sys.unsetenv("RUN_DIR"));
  rmarkdown::render(inputFile, encoding = encoding,
                    output_file = "Analysis.html",
                    output_dir = out);
  })
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    toc_float:
      collapsed: true
      smooth_scroll: true
    code_folding: hide
---

## Before you run this file

**USER ACTION REQUIRED:** Edit the values in the first code chunk below. All dataset-specific settings are grouped there and marked with `USER MUST SPECIFY`. The example values come from the KPWA anaphylaxis analysis and can be replaced with values for another cohort.

The input must have one row per patient and numeric, nonnegative model
variables. Count variables should remain untransformed because stage 1 applies
`log(x + 1)`. The chart-reviewed rows must contain both 0 and 1 outcomes.
Unreviewed rows are used to train PheNorm; reviewed rows are used for internal
evaluation.

The input is read from a `.csv` file.

```{r user-configuration}
# ============================================================================
# EDIT THIS SECTION BEFORE RUNNING A NEW ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

# Data path ---------------------------------------------------------------
# USER MUST SPECIFY: either an absolute path or a path built with here::here().
data_file <- here::here("Data", "Smoke_test", "phenorm_smoke_test_nonrare_info.csv")

# Dataset columns ---------------------------------------------------------
# USER MUST SPECIFY: a unique patient/row identifier column.
study_id_col <- "study_id"

# USER MUST SPECIFY: column identifying chart-reviewed/evaluation rows, and the value in that column that means "reviewed". All other nonmissing values are treated as unreviewed/training rows.
reviewed_col <- "reviewed_col"
reviewed_value <- 1

# USER MUST SPECIFY: binary gold-standard outcome column (0 = negative, 1 = positive). It may be missing for unreviewed rows, but not reviewed rows.
gold_outcome_col <- "gold_outcome"

# USER MUST SPECIFY: nonnegative utilization variable (for example, number of notes or encounters). PheNorm uses it for normalization.
utilization_col <- "utilization"

# USER MUST SPECIFY, or use NULL: inverse-probability/sample-weight column.
# When NULL, every row receives weight 1.
sampling_weight_col <- "sampling_weight"

# Model variables ---------------------------------------------------------
# USER MUST SPECIFY: the exact silver-label column names. At least one is
# required, and every name must begin with the lowercase prefix "silver_".
silver_label_cols <- c(
  "silver_total_icd_nlp",
  "silver_total_icd_mention",
  "silver_total_nlp"
)

# USER MUST SPECIFY: every other predictor column, exactly by name. List Race
# and CUI columns individually here; regular-expression extraction is not used.
# Do not repeat the ID, review indicator, outcome, utilization, weight, or
# silver-label columns here.
predictor_cols <- c(
  "age", "sex_female",
  "race_asian", "race_black", "race_white",
  "C0000001", "C0000002"
)

# Analysis settings -------------------------------------------------------
# USER MUST SPECIFY: a short site/cohort name used in output filenames.
# Use only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.
site <- "smoke_test"

# OPTIONAL: stage-4 prediction sites. Keep both equal to `site` to use the
# analysis data and fitted model created in this run. For cross-site prediction,
# set the data/model sites separately and provide the corresponding directories.
stage4_data_site <- site
stage4_model_site <- site

# OPTIONAL: directories used only by stage 4.
# `stage4_data_dir` must contain:
#   <analysis_name>_<stage4_data_site>_analysis_data.rds
# `stage4_output_dir` must contain:
#   fits/<analysis_name>_<stage4_model_site>_phenorm_output.rds
# NULL uses this run's analysis-data and results directories, respectively.
stage4_data_dir <- NULL
stage4_output_dir <- NULL

# OPTIONAL: output name stem. NULL uses this Rmd file's name.
analysis_id <- NULL

```

## Setup

Reports, results, and logs are saved in a timestamped folder in the project's
`Result` directory. Prepared and analysis-ready data use a matching folder
under `Result/Processed_data`.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)

project_dir <- here::here()
analysis_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "Result")

current_input <- knitr::current_input()
analysis_name <- if (!is.null(analysis_id)) {
  analysis_id
} else if (length(current_input) == 1L && nzchar(current_input)) {
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(current_input))
} else {
  # Fallback for running individual chunks outside a Knit/render operation.
  "Generalizable_PheNorm_Analysis"
}

if (!is.character(analysis_name) || length(analysis_name) != 1L ||
    !nzchar(analysis_name) || !grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$", analysis_name)) {
  stop("analysis_id must contain only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.")
}
site_settings <- list(
  site = site,
  stage4_data_site = stage4_data_site,
  stage4_model_site = stage4_model_site
)
valid_site <- function(x) {
  is.character(x) && length(x) == 1L && nzchar(x) &&
    grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$", x)
}
invalid_sites <- names(site_settings)[
  !vapply(site_settings, valid_site, logical(1))
]
if (length(invalid_sites)) {
  stop(
    paste(invalid_sites, collapse = ", "),
    " must contain only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens."
  )
}

# Use the directory created by the custom Knit function. When chunks are run
# interactively or rmarkdown::render() is called directly, create a new one.
run_dir <- Sys.getenv("RUN_DIR")
if (!nzchar(run_dir)) {
  run_dir <- file.path(
    analysis_dir,
    paste0(analysis_name, "_result_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
  )
}

processed_data_run_dir <- file.path(
  analysis_dir, "Processed_data", basename(run_dir)
)

dirs <- c(
  file.path(processed_data_run_dir, c("prepared_input", "analysis_data")),
  file.path(run_dir, c("results", "logs"))
)
names(dirs) <- c("input", "analysis", "results", "logs")
invisible(lapply(dirs, dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))
slash <- function(x) paste0(normalizePath(x), "/")

stage4_data_dir_resolved <- if (is.null(stage4_data_dir)) {
  dirs[["analysis"]]
} else {
  stage4_data_dir
}
stage4_output_dir_resolved <- if (is.null(stage4_output_dir)) {
  dirs[["results"]]
} else {
  stage4_output_dir
}
if (!dir.exists(stage4_data_dir_resolved)) {
  stop("stage4_data_dir does not exist: ", stage4_data_dir_resolved)
}
if (!dir.exists(stage4_output_dir_resolved)) {
  stop("stage4_output_dir does not exist: ", stage4_output_dir_resolved)
}
```

## Phenorm analysis

### Prepare the cohort

The following code maps the user-selected source columns to the standardized
special-purpose names expected by the unchanged PheNorm scripts. Predictor
names are retained. Silver-label source columns are selected only from the
explicit list above; when necessary, their names are prefixed internally with
`SILVER_` because stage 1 identifies silver labels by that word.

```{r prepare-cohort}
# Read the data.
if (!file.exists(data_file)) stop("Data file does not exist: ", data_file)
raw <- read.csv(
  data_file,
  check.names = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("NA", ".", "")
)

if (!is.data.frame(raw)) stop("The input must be a data frame.")
if (nrow(raw) == 0L) stop("The input data has no rows.")
if (anyDuplicated(names(raw))) stop("The input has duplicated column names.")

# Validate the explicitly supplied model columns.
if (!is.character(predictor_cols) || !is.character(silver_label_cols) ||
    length(silver_label_cols) == 0L) {
  stop("predictor_cols and silver_label_cols must be character vectors; at least one silver label is required.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(silver_label_cols) || any(!nzchar(silver_label_cols))) {
  stop("silver_label_cols must contain unique, nonempty column names.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(predictor_cols) || any(!nzchar(predictor_cols))) {
  stop("predictor_cols must contain unique, nonempty column names.")
}

# Validate configured source columns before subsetting.
required_cols <- c(
  reviewed_col, gold_outcome_col, utilization_col, silver_label_cols,
  predictor_cols
)
if (!is.null(study_id_col)) required_cols <- c(required_cols, study_id_col)
if (!is.null(sampling_weight_col)) {
  required_cols <- c(required_cols, sampling_weight_col)
}
missing_cols <- setdiff(unique(required_cols), names(raw))
if (length(missing_cols)) {
  stop("Configured columns not found in the data: ",
       paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
}

special_cols <- unique(c(
  study_id_col, reviewed_col, gold_outcome_col, utilization_col,
  sampling_weight_col, silver_label_cols
))
overlap <- intersect(predictor_cols, special_cols)
if (length(overlap)) {
  stop("Remove these special-purpose columns from predictor_cols: ",
       paste(overlap, collapse = ", "))
}

# Cohort setup: unreviewed rows train the model; reviewed rows evaluate it.
reviewed_raw <- raw[[reviewed_col]]
if (anyNA(reviewed_raw)) stop("The review indicator contains missing values.")
reviewed <- reviewed_raw == reviewed_value
if (!any(reviewed) || !any(!reviewed)) {
  stop("The data must contain both reviewed/evaluation and unreviewed/training rows.")
}

outcome <- raw[[gold_outcome_col]]
if (!is.numeric(outcome) && !is.integer(outcome) && !is.logical(outcome)) {
  stop("The gold-standard outcome must be numeric/logical and coded 0/1.")
}
reviewed_outcomes <- as.numeric(outcome[reviewed])
if (anyNA(reviewed_outcomes) || any(!reviewed_outcomes %in% 0:1) ||
    !identical(sort(unique(reviewed_outcomes)), c(0, 1))) {
  stop("Reviewed outcomes must be nonmissing and include both 0 and 1.")
}

study_id <- if (is.null(study_id_col)) seq_len(nrow(raw)) else raw[[study_id_col]]
sampling_weight <- if (is.null(sampling_weight_col)) {
  rep(1, nrow(raw))
} else {
  raw[[sampling_weight_col]]
}

# Map source silver labels to the uppercase internal names expected downstream.
silver_model_names <- toupper(ifelse(
  grepl("silver", silver_label_cols, ignore.case = TRUE),
  silver_label_cols,
  paste0("SILVER_", make.names(silver_label_cols))
))
silver_model_names <- make.unique(silver_model_names)

feature_cols <- c(predictor_cols, silver_label_cols)
feature_data <- raw[feature_cols]
names(feature_data)[match(silver_label_cols, names(feature_data))] <-
  silver_model_names
reserved_model_names <- c(
  "Studyid", "Train_Eval_Set", "PTYPE_POSITIVE", "Sampling_Weight", "Utiliz"
)
name_collisions <- intersect(names(feature_data), reserved_model_names)
if (length(name_collisions) || anyDuplicated(names(feature_data))) {
  stop(
    "Selected predictors produce duplicated/reserved prepared-data names: ",
    paste(unique(c(name_collisions,
                   names(feature_data)[duplicated(names(feature_data))])),
          collapse = ", ")
  )
}

cohort <- data.frame(
  Studyid = study_id,
  Train_Eval_Set = as.integer(reviewed),
  PTYPE_POSITIVE = ifelse(reviewed, as.integer(outcome), NA_integer_),
  Sampling_Weight = sampling_weight,
  Utiliz = if (is.null(utilization_col)) 1 else raw[[utilization_col]],
  feature_data,
  check.names = FALSE
)

model_data <- cohort[setdiff(names(cohort), c("Studyid", "PTYPE_POSITIVE"))]
if (anyDuplicated(cohort$Studyid) || anyNA(cohort$Studyid)) {
  stop("Study IDs must be unique and nonmissing.")
}
if (!all(vapply(model_data, is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
  bad <- names(model_data)[!vapply(model_data, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  stop("All model variables must be numeric. Recode: ",
       paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
}
if (anyNA(model_data) || !all(is.finite(as.matrix(model_data)))) {
  stop("Model variables must be complete and finite (no NA, NaN, or Inf).")
}
if (any(as.matrix(model_data) < 0)) {
  stop("Model variables must be nonnegative.")
}
if (any(cohort$Sampling_Weight <= 0)) {
  stop("Sampling weights must be greater than zero.")
}

input_file <- file.path(
  dirs[["input"]],
  paste0(analysis_name, "_prepared.rds")
)
saveRDS(cohort, input_file)
```

### Run the PheNorm pipeline

Each stage runs in a separate R process. Output is shown here and saved in the
run's `logs` folder; a failed stage stops the notebook.

```{r run-pipeline}
run_stage <- function(name, script, args) {
  old_wd <- setwd(project_dir)
  on.exit(setwd(old_wd))
  output <- system2(
    file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
    c(shQuote(file.path(project_dir, "PheNorm", script)),
      vapply(args, shQuote, character(1))),
    stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE
  )
  status <- attr(output, "status")
  if (is.null(status)) status <- 0L
  log_file <- file.path(dirs["logs"], paste0(name, ".log"))
  writeLines(output, log_file)
  if (status != 0L) stop(name, " failed; see ", log_file, "\n",
                         paste(output, collapse = "\n"))
  data.frame(Stage = name, Exit_status = status, Log = log_file)
}
```

### Stage 1: process the input data

The following settings control Stage 1 preprocessing and feature selection.

```{r stage-1-tuning-parameters}
# Define and display the Stage 1 tuning parameters passed to preprocessing.
stage1_afep_cui <- "C5203670"
stage1_use_afep <- FALSE
stage1_use_nonnegative_mentions <- FALSE
stage1_nonnegative_label <- "_nonneg"
stage1_use_nonnormalized_features <- TRUE
stage1_use_normalized_features <- FALSE
stage1_train_on_gold <- FALSE
stage1_chart_reviewed <- TRUE

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Tuning_parameter = c(
    "stage1_afep_cui",
    "stage1_use_afep",
    "stage1_use_nonnegative_mentions",
    "stage1_nonnegative_label",
    "stage1_use_nonnormalized_features",
    "stage1_use_normalized_features",
    "stage1_train_on_gold",
    "stage1_chart_reviewed"
  ),
  Value = c(
    stage1_afep_cui,
    stage1_use_afep,
    stage1_use_nonnegative_mentions,
    stage1_nonnegative_label,
    stage1_use_nonnormalized_features,
    stage1_use_normalized_features,
    stage1_train_on_gold,
    stage1_chart_reviewed
  ),
  Meaning = c(
    "Outcome-specific CUI used if AFEP screening is enabled",
    "Apply AFEP screening to NLP variables",
    "Use non-negated mentions instead of all mentions",
    "Suffix identifying non-negated CUI variables",
    "Include non-normalized NLP features",
    "Include normalized NLP features",
    "Include chart-reviewed observations in model training",
    "Indicate that gold-standard chart reviews are available"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
))

stage1_afep_flag <- if (stage1_use_afep) "--use-afep" else "--no-afep"
stage1_nonnegative_flag <- if (stage1_use_nonnegative_mentions) {
  "--use-nonneg"
} else {
  "--no-nonneg"
}
stage1_nonnormalized_flag <- if (stage1_use_nonnormalized_features) {
  "--use-nonnormalized"
} else {
  "--no-nonnormalized"
}
stage1_normalized_flag <- if (stage1_use_normalized_features) {
  "--use-normalized"
} else {
  "--no-normalized"
}
stage1_train_on_gold_flag <- if (stage1_train_on_gold) {
  "--train-on-gold"
} else {
  character(0)
}
```

```{r process-data}
stage_1 <- run_stage(
  "01_process_data",
  "01_process_data.R",
  c(
    "--data-dir", slash(dirs["input"]),
    "--analysis-data-dir", slash(dirs["analysis"]),
    "--data-name", basename(input_file),
    "--analysis", analysis_name,
    "--train-value", "Training",
    "--gold-label", "PTYPE_POSITIVE",
    "--valid-label", "Train_Eval_Set",
    "--study-id", "Studyid",
    "--utilization", "Utiliz",
    "--weight", "Sampling_Weight",
    "--site", site,
    "--cui", stage1_afep_cui,
    "--nonneg-label", stage1_nonnegative_label,
    "--chart-reviewed", as.character(stage1_chart_reviewed),
    stage1_nonnegative_flag,
    stage1_afep_flag,
    stage1_nonnormalized_flag,
    stage1_normalized_flag,
    stage1_train_on_gold_flag
  )
)
knitr::kable(stage_1)
```

### Stage 2: fit PheNorm

The following settings control PheNorm fitting and its random resampling.

```{r stage-2-tuning-parameters}
# Define and display the Stage 2 tuning parameters passed to model fitting.
stage2_seed <- 12345L
stage2_corrupt_rate <- 0.3
stage2_train_size_multiplier <- 13L

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Tuning_parameter = c(
    "stage2_seed",
    "stage2_corrupt_rate",
    "stage2_train_size_multiplier"
  ),
  Value = c(
    stage2_seed,
    stage2_corrupt_rate,
    stage2_train_size_multiplier
  ),
  Meaning = c(
    "Random-number seed used for reproducible fitting",
    "Probability used for random corruption during denoising",
    "Multiplier used to determine the resampled training size"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

```{r fit-phenorm}
stage_2 <- run_stage(
  "02_run_phenorm",
  "02_run_phenorm.R",
  c(
    "--data-dir", slash(dirs["analysis"]),
    "--output-dir", slash(dirs["results"]),
    "--analysis", analysis_name,

    "--weight", "Sampling_Weight",

  )
)
knitr::kable(stage_2)
```

### Stage 4: predict the full cohort

The original stage-4 script registers `--seed` twice, so this analysis uses the
documented modified copy, as in the reference notebook. When the stage-4 data
or model site differs from `site`, the configured directories must contain the
analysis-data and fitted-model files described in the configuration section.

Stage 4 uses the following reproducibility setting when generating full-cohort
predictions.

```{r stage-4-tuning-parameters}
# Define and display the Stage 4 tuning parameters passed to prediction.

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Tuning_parameter = "stage4_seed",
  Value = stage4_seed,

  check.names = FALSE
))
```

## Results

The following summaries are produced only after all four pipeline stages
complete. The opening tables provide a high-level view of the data and analysis;
the remaining subsections give supporting performance and diagnostic results.

### Analysis overview

This table summarizes the dataset dimensions, chart-review sampling, gold
standard composition, and predictor types used in the analysis.

```{r analysis-overview}
n_total <- nrow(raw)
n_reviewed <- sum(reviewed)
n_unreviewed <- sum(!reviewed)
n_cases <- sum(outcome[reviewed] == 1)
n_controls <- sum(outcome[reviewed] == 0)
nlp_predictors <- grepl("^C[0-9]+$", predictor_cols)
model_feature_cols <- unique(c(predictor_cols, silver_label_cols))
complete_unreviewed_model_features <-
  !reviewed & complete.cases(raw[model_feature_cols])
reviewed_complete_cols <- unique(c(model_feature_cols, gold_outcome_col))
complete_reviewed_model_features_and_gold <-
  reviewed & complete.cases(raw[reviewed_complete_cols])

analysis_overview <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Input dataset dimensions",
    "Unreviewed observations complete for predictors and silver labels",
    "Chart-reviewed observations complete for predictors, silver labels, and gold standard",
    "Chart-reviewed observations",
    "Unreviewed training observations",
    "Gold-standard cases",
    "Gold-standard controls",
    "Silver-label variables",
    "Structured predictors",
    "CUI-based NLP predictors",
    "Sampling-weight range"
  ),
  Result = c(
    paste0(format(n_total, big.mark = ","), " observations × ",
           ncol(raw), " variables"),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%% of unreviewed)",
            format(sum(complete_unreviewed_model_features), big.mark = ","),
            100 * sum(complete_unreviewed_model_features) / n_unreviewed),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%% of reviewed)",
            format(sum(complete_reviewed_model_features_and_gold), big.mark = ","),
            100 * sum(complete_reviewed_model_features_and_gold) / n_reviewed),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(n_reviewed, big.mark = ","),
            100 * n_reviewed / n_total),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(n_unreviewed, big.mark = ","),
            100 * n_unreviewed / n_total),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%% of reviewed)", format(n_cases, big.mark = ","),
            100 * n_cases / n_reviewed),
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%% of reviewed)", format(n_controls, big.mark = ","),
            100 * n_controls / n_reviewed),
    length(silver_label_cols),
    sum(!nlp_predictors),
    sum(nlp_predictors),
    sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(sampling_weight), max(sampling_weight))
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  analysis_overview,
  caption = paste(
    "Complete-case rows assess the configured predictors and silver labels",
    "for unreviewed observations, and those fields plus the gold-standard",
    "outcome for chart-reviewed observations. Utilization and sampling-weight",
    "fields are not included, but could be added for a broader assessment of",
    "pipeline readiness."
  )
)
```

### Silver-label summary

The first table describes the distribution and sparsity of each silver label
in the full cohort. Count variables are summarized on their original input
scale, before the pipeline's `log(x + 1)` transformation.

```{r silver-label-summary}
summarize_silver <- function(x) {
  data.frame(
    Nonzero_rows = sum(x > 0),
    Nonzero_percent = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(x > 0)),
    `Mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

silver_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(silver_label_cols, function(label) {
  data.frame(
    Silver_label = label,
    summarize_silver(raw[[label]]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(silver_summary)
```

The next table compares silver-label distributions between cases and controls
within the chart-reviewed gold-standard sample. Large differences between the
groups indicate that a silver label contains useful phenotyping signal.

```{r silver-label-by-gold-status}
reviewed_groups <- list(
  Cases = reviewed & outcome == 1,
  Controls = reviewed & outcome == 0
)
silver_by_gold <- do.call(rbind, lapply(silver_label_cols, function(label) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(reviewed_groups), function(group) {
    x <- raw[[label]][reviewed_groups[[group]]]
    data.frame(
      Silver_label = label,
      Gold_standard_group = group,
      N = length(x),
      Nonzero_percent = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(x > 0)),
      `Mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x)),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(silver_by_gold)
```

The boxplots visualize the complete silver-label distributions among reviewed
cases and controls. Values are displayed as `log(silver label + 1)` so that
right-skewed count distributions and zero values remain visible.

```{r silver-label-boxplots}
silver_plot_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(silver_label_cols, function(label) {
  data.frame(
    Silver_label = label,
    Gold_standard_group = factor(
      ifelse(outcome[reviewed] == 1, "Cases", "Controls"),
      levels = c("Controls", "Cases")
    ),
    Silver_value = raw[[label]][reviewed],
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(
  silver_plot_data,
  aes(x = Gold_standard_group, y = log1p(Silver_value),
      fill = Gold_standard_group)
) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Silver_label), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Controls" = "#4C78A8", "Cases" = "#E45756")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "log(silver label + 1)",
    title = "Silver-label distributions by gold-standard outcome",
    subtitle = "Chart-reviewed evaluation sample"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Source names are mapped to uppercase internal names for compatibility with the
downstream PheNorm scripts.

```{r silver-label-name-mapping}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Source_silver_label = silver_label_cols,
  Internal_silver_label = silver_model_names
))
```

### Internal validation performance

The table compares each raw silver label with its fitted PheNorm model on the
held-out chart-reviewed sample. The aggregate model averages predictions from
all silver-label-specific models and therefore has no single raw-label result.
Larger AUC values indicate better ranking of cases above non-cases.

```{r auc-results}
result_prefix <- file.path(
  dirs["results"], "plots_and_tables",
  paste0(
    "phenorm_", analysis_name, "_data_", site,
    "_model_", site
  )
)
auc_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_aucs.csv")
raw_auc_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_raw_silver_aucs.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(auc_file), file.exists(raw_auc_file))

auc_results <- read.csv(auc_file, check.names = FALSE)
raw_auc_results <- read.csv(raw_auc_file, check.names = FALSE)
label_map <- setNames(silver_label_cols, silver_model_names)
display_model_name <- function(x) {
  mapped <- unname(label_map[x])
  ifelse(x == "Aggregate", "Aggregate",
         ifelse(is.na(mapped), x, mapped))
}
auc_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = display_model_name(auc_results$id),
  `PheNorm AUC [95% CI]` = auc_results$est_ci,
  `Raw silver AUC [95% CI]` = raw_auc_results$est_ci[
    match(auc_results$id, raw_auc_results$id)
  ],
  check.names = FALSE
)
auc_comparison[["Raw silver AUC [95% CI]"]][
  is.na(auc_comparison[["Raw silver AUC [95% CI]"]])
] <- "Not applicable"
knitr::kable(auc_comparison)
```

#### Performance at the maximum-F1 cutoff

This table reports the cutoff selected to maximize F1 within the evaluation
sample, together with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and F
scores at that cutoff.

```{r maximum-f1-results}
max_f1_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_max_f1.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(max_f1_file))
max_f1_results <- read.csv(max_f1_file, check.names = FALSE)
max_f1_results$id <- display_model_name(max_f1_results$id)
names(max_f1_results)[names(max_f1_results) == "id"] <- "Model"
numeric_f1_cols <- vapply(max_f1_results, is.numeric, logical(1))
max_f1_results[numeric_f1_cols] <- lapply(
  max_f1_results[numeric_f1_cols], round, 3
)
knitr::kable(max_f1_results)
```

#### Held-out ROC curves

The combined ROC plot shows sensitivity versus one minus specificity across
all thresholds for each silver-label model and the aggregate model. Curves
closer to the upper-left corner indicate stronger discrimination.

```{r combined-roc}
roc_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_combined_roc.png")
stopifnot(file.exists(roc_file))
knitr::include_graphics(roc_file)
```

### Full-cohort prediction diagnostics

The prediction file is checked for completeness, finite values, and valid
probability bounds. For a same-site run, the plot then compares aggregate
predicted probabilities between gold-standard cases and non-cases in the
held-out evaluation sample. Better separation supports the discrimination
summarized by the ROC results above.

```{r load-predictions, include=FALSE}
prediction_file <- file.path(
  stage4_output_dir_resolved, "fits",
  paste0(
    analysis_name, "_", stage4_data_site,
    "_phenorm_all_predicted_probabilities_using_", stage4_model_site,
    "_model.csv"
  )
)
stopifnot(file.exists(prediction_file))

predictions <- read.csv(prediction_file, check.names = FALSE)
probabilities <- predictions[setdiff(names(predictions), "Studyid")]
stopifnot(
  ncol(probabilities) >= 1L,
  "Aggregate" %in% names(probabilities),
  !anyNA(probabilities),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(probabilities))),
  all(as.matrix(probabilities) >= 0 & as.matrix(probabilities) <= 1)
)

plot_data <- NULL
if (identical(stage4_data_site, site)) {
  stopifnot(
    nrow(predictions) == nrow(cohort),
    ncol(probabilities) == length(silver_label_cols) + 1L
  )
  plot_data <- cbind(
    cohort[c("Studyid", "Train_Eval_Set", "PTYPE_POSITIVE")],
    probabilities
  )
  plot_data <- plot_data[plot_data$Train_Eval_Set == 1L, ]
  plot_data$Outcome <- factor(
    plot_data$PTYPE_POSITIVE,
    levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c("Negative", "Positive")
  )
}
```

The table summarizes aggregate predicted probabilities across the full cohort
and, for a same-site analysis, separately for reviewed cases and controls.

```{r prediction-summary}
summarize_predictions <- function(x, population) {
  data.frame(
    Population = population,
    N = length(x),
    Mean = mean(x),
    SD = sd(x),
    Median = median(x),
    Q1 = unname(quantile(x, 0.25)),
    Q3 = unname(quantile(x, 0.75)),
    Min = min(x),
    Max = max(x),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
prediction_summary <- summarize_predictions(
  probabilities$Aggregate, "Full cohort"
)
if (!is.null(plot_data)) {
  prediction_summary <- rbind(
    prediction_summary,
    summarize_predictions(
      plot_data$Aggregate[plot_data$Outcome == "Positive"],
      "Reviewed cases"
    ),
    summarize_predictions(
      plot_data$Aggregate[plot_data$Outcome == "Negative"],
      "Reviewed controls"
    )
  )
}
numeric_prediction_cols <- vapply(prediction_summary, is.numeric, logical(1))
numeric_prediction_cols["N"] <- FALSE
prediction_summary[numeric_prediction_cols] <- lapply(
  prediction_summary[numeric_prediction_cols], round, 3
)
knitr::kable(prediction_summary)
```

```{r probability-by-class}
if (is.null(plot_data)) {
  cat(
    "Prediction diagnostic plot skipped because stage4_data_site differs ",
    "from the cohort prepared in this notebook.\n",
    sep = ""
  )
} else {
  library(ggplot2)
  print(
    ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = Outcome, y = Aggregate, fill = Outcome)
    ) +

      geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +

      labs(
        x = NULL,

        title = "PheNorm predictions by gold-standard outcome",
        subtitle = "Held-out evaluation set"
      ) +

}
```

### Model interpretation

Permutation importance measures the decrease in evaluation AUC after one
variable is randomly permuted. The table shows up to ten variables with the
largest absolute importance for the aggregate prediction, excluding pipeline
identifier and outcome fields.

```{r variable-importance-results}
vim_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_vim.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(vim_file))
vim_results <- read.csv(vim_file, check.names = FALSE)
excluded_vim_variables <- toupper(c(
  "Studyid", "Train_Eval_Set", "PTYPE_POSITIVE", "Sampling_Weight"
))
vim_results <- vim_results[
  !(toupper(vim_results$var) %in% excluded_vim_variables),
  , drop = FALSE
]
vim_results <- vim_results[
  order(abs(vim_results$est_Aggregate), decreasing = TRUE),
  , drop = FALSE
]
vim_display <- head(vim_results[c("var", "est_Aggregate")], 10L)
names(vim_display) <- c("Variable", "Aggregate AUC decrease")
vim_display[["Aggregate AUC decrease"]] <- round(
  vim_display[["Aggregate AUC decrease"]], 4
)
knitr::kable(vim_display)
```

The coefficient table shows up to ten variables with the largest absolute
coefficient in any silver-label-specific PheNorm model. Signs indicate the
direction of association with the corresponding normalized phenotype score.

```{r coefficient-results}
coefficient_file <- paste0(result_prefix, "_coefficients.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(coefficient_file))
coefficient_results <- read.csv(coefficient_file, check.names = FALSE)
coefficient_numeric <- vapply(coefficient_results, is.numeric, logical(1))
coefficient_rank <- apply(
  abs(as.matrix(coefficient_results[coefficient_numeric])), 1, max
)
coefficient_results <- coefficient_results[
  order(coefficient_rank, decreasing = TRUE),
  , drop = FALSE
]
coefficient_display <- head(coefficient_results, 10L)
coefficient_display[coefficient_numeric] <- lapply(
  coefficient_display[coefficient_numeric], round, 3
)
knitr::kable(coefficient_display)
```

The data-quality checks summarize issues that could affect interpretation. A
successful run has no duplicate IDs, missing required model values, nonfinite
values, or negative model values.

```{r data-quality-summary}
quality_cols <- unique(c(
  reviewed_col, utilization_col, sampling_weight_col,
  silver_label_cols, predictor_cols
))
quality_data <- raw[quality_cols]
numeric_quality_data <- quality_data[
  vapply(quality_data, is.numeric, logical(1))
]
data_quality <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Duplicate study IDs",
    "Missing values in required model fields",
    "Missing gold outcomes among reviewed observations",
    "Nonfinite numeric model values",
    "Negative numeric model values",
    "Nonpositive sampling weights",
    "Zero-variance selected predictors",
    "Pipeline stages completed successfully"
  ),
  Result = c(
    anyDuplicated(study_id),
    sum(is.na(quality_data)),
    sum(is.na(outcome[reviewed])),
    sum(!is.finite(as.matrix(numeric_quality_data))),
    sum(as.matrix(numeric_quality_data) < 0),
    sum(sampling_weight <= 0),
    sum(vapply(raw[predictor_cols], function(x) length(unique(x)) <= 1L,
               logical(1))),
    all(c(stage_1$Exit_status, stage_2$Exit_status, stage_3$Exit_status,
          stage_4$Exit_status) == 0L)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(data_quality)
```
